sources.anchor: dedicated intent folders; intent and shape for each; no implementation
I want the landing page to speak to a developer who might embed my comp in their existing data analysis tool.  Or they are makign their own analysis platform and want my stuff as a primtive.
It will become major once it is working.  Agent driven BI and data viz is powerful stuff

THe add and edit on charts is most important. That action is done countless times a day by people.  Calcs are important but less critical since they tend to be "Set nad forget" when things are saved well.
I think they start with an example.  If they offer their own data, they likelyl start from scratch on that
Probably start fresh?  Not a strong opinion.  If we store it, we need to make it easy to reset.

I think very minimal.  Waht we really need is a detailed "chart spec" screen that list all teh charts, their positions, tehir config.  That way users can see all teh details without seeing JSON.  They could even tweak things there.  But mainly they can see that charts are driven by config.
I guess suggest 5 tangible things here.  I am struggling to see what htis would be.

Given all this, let's assume taht everything stays "single source" for now.  Clearly multiple sources is its own project.  Maybe we cna go ahead adn run $sleuth to get that separate intent/shape built.

It seems we should be able to store snapshots of the settings as changes are made.  We could diff that and show it.  Or just undo.  It's not clear to me why undo is difficult if state is fully determined by the settings?  What am i missing?
The first 3 are great and would be nice additions.

claims.statement: The landing page primarily serves developers embedding the component or building an analysis platform.
Explore an example is the primary landing action.
The agent story becomes major once integrated assistance works.
Adding and editing charts have greater demonstration value than calculations.
Visitors start with an example; personal data starts a fresh analysis.
Example visits probably start fresh; retained edits require easy Reset.
A readable chart spec screen lists all charts, positions, and configuration, with minimal JSON exposure.
The chart spec screen may support edits; inspection is the primary requirement.
This initiative remains single-source; multiple sources have a separate scope.
Provide five concrete examples of live-settings inspection: inventory, details, referenced definitions, snapshot comparison, and host access.
claims.notes: Five suggested uses requested for clarification; these are not five mandatory new features.

claims.statement: Include chart inventory, detailed settings, and expandable referenced calculation and color-scale definitions.
Embedding hosts can read the same current analysis settings for their own inspector or agent.
Defer settings change-comparison UI. Snapshot Undo does not require it.

shape.appetite: Focused developer landing journey plus chart spec inspection; spec editing optional.
shape.recommended_shape: Use the existing live example as the primary entry for developers evaluating the component. Demonstrate adding and editing charts. Provide chart inventory, detailed settings, and expandable referenced definitions in a readable chart spec screen. Expose the same current settings to embedding hosts. Keep JSON in optional integration detail.
success_moves: Read live settings in the spec screen

first_proof.question: Can developers inspect runtime configuration without reading JSON?
first_proof.artifact: A reviewed chart add/edit and specification journey
first_proof.decision_rule: Chart inventory, details, and referenced definitions match runtime state; host reads agree initially and after edits.

review.remaining_weaknesses: The readable spec screen is new scope. A partial summary that omits positions or configuration would miss its purpose. Spec editing is a possibility, not an acceptance requirement. Example persistence remains a reversible choice with a reset requirement if retained.
review.most_likely_bad_outcome: A polished landing page shows fixed examples and a JSON dump, while developers still cannot see how users create and revise charts.
